verdict_rationale: The v4 crate additions (4 crates + 1 binary + Cedar + registry/accounts/) are trivially reversible — all additive, Branch Y, zero existing-kernel surface change. The F10 gap is entirely in v5's settings-template renderer: dotfile writes to ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/hooks.json, ~/.gemini/settings.json are NOT auto-reverted by a code rollback, and no kill-switch guards the render path. VerifyMode::FailOnDrift is hardwired at SupervisorApp::new() with no env-var bypass, creating a workspace-wide blackhole path if the canonical template drifts all accounts simultaneously. Three mandatory remediations (F10-01, F10-02, F10-03) must land before merge.

findings.title: Settings renderer hardwired into SupervisorApp::new — no kill-switch for dotfile writes
findings.evidence: v5 §B.4 shows CompositeAccountSnapshotProvider::with_verify(renderers, template_root, home_dir, VerifyMode::FailOnDrift) passed directly to SupervisorApp::new(...). No env-var, no SupervisorConfig field, no RendererMode enum guards this path. If the renderer writes malformed content to ~/.claude/settings.json after merge, reverting the code does not restore the dotfile. Every machine running the supervisor accumulates the damage until manual restoration. The VerifyMode::AutoReconcile variant (v5 §B.4) is an even higher-risk codepath — auto-writing settings on every snapshot() call — and it is equally ungated.
artifact_refs: v5-§B.2.2: SettingsRenderer::render signature (no dry-run mode declared)
v4-§B.2.5: SupervisorConfig fields (watchdog_secs, heartbeat_interval_secs — no renderer_mode field)
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: Code revert removes the renderer binary but leaves previously-written settings in ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/hooks.json, ~/.gemini/settings.json. Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI continue reading the renderer-written settings until manually restored. Hooks installed by the renderer continue firing even after supervisor is reverted.
findings.remediation: Add RendererMode { Disabled, VerifyOnly, Reconcile } to SupervisorConfig. Default = Disabled for first release cycle. Promote to VerifyOnly once C.25..C.30 are green in production for ≥1 sprint. Gate Reconcile behind an explicit env-var OYA_SETTINGS_RECONCILE=1. This ensures a no-op rollback path at any phase.

findings.title: No backup-before-write; dotfile mutations survive code rollback with no recovery path
findings.evidence: v5 §B.2.2 describes atomic tempfile+rename(2) for each rendered file — this guarantees write atomicity but does NOT preserve the prior file content. Neither v4 nor v5 document a backup mechanism (e.g., target_path + '.omc-bak-<epoch>') before overwriting ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.codex/hooks.json. Acceptance rows C.25..C.30 have no row testing 'renderer produces recoverable output; previous state restorable.' Compare: v4 §A.4 scenario (a) documents crash-injection + recovery for inbox/outbox (tests/crash_injection.rs), but no equivalent 'undo-render' recovery exists for the dotfile mutation path.
artifact_refs: v5-§B.2.2: 'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2). Idempotent.' — idempotency covers repeated correct writes, not bad-content recovery
v5-§C.25..C.30: no acceptance row covering dotfile rollback or backup restoration
v4-§A.4 scenario (a): crash-injection precedent for inbox/outbox recovery (absent for settings)
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: After code revert the supervisor stops rendering settings. But ~/.claude/settings.json (and equivalents) retain whatever the renderer last wrote. If the renderer had a bug (e.g., incorrect hook event names, wrong mcp_servers keys), all three CLIs continue reading bad settings indefinitely. The user has no documented path to restore the pre-render state.
findings.remediation: Before each render(target_path), check if the file exists and copy it to target_path + '.omc-settings-bak.' + epoch_secs. Provide tools/undo-settings-render.sh that finds .omc-settings-bak.* files per provider and restores them. Add acceptance row C.31: undo-settings-render.sh restores original content byte-for-byte (verified by sha256 comparison). This script is the migration_rollback_script_path that is currently null.

findings.title: VerifyMode::FailOnDrift silently blackholes all accounts; failure indistinguishable from 'no accounts configured'
findings.evidence: v5 §B.4: 'If VerifyMode::FailOnDrift and any account's DriftReport.entries contains a non-Match state, the account is excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>.' If ALL accounts drift simultaneously (e.g., after a SettingsTemplate.version bump per v5 §B.2.1 without a preceding auto-reconcile pass), snapshot() returns []. This cascades: v4 §B.4 step 4 (RoutePolicy::select(&accounts, &constraints)) receives zero candidates and returns NoEligibleAccount. Every tick_once call fails. The v4 TickOutcome enum (v4 §B.2.5: Spawned/Saturated/Idle/Quarantined) has no DriftExcluded variant — callers cannot distinguish 'no accounts registered' from 'all accounts drift-excluded'. This is a workspace-wide silent outage.
artifact_refs: v5-§B.4: 'account is excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>' — no minimum-eligible-accounts guard
v5-§B.2.1: SettingsTemplate.version u32 — a version bump is a forward step that causes global drift
v4-§B.2.5: TickOutcome enum lacks DriftExcluded variant
v4-§B.4 step 4: RoutePolicy::select fails on empty accounts slice
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: Reverting v5 restores the old snapshot provider (which does not do drift verification) and unfreezes routing. However, the interval during which all accounts were drift-excluded produced no messages processed — those inbox messages are stuck in Locked state (TTL eventually releases them per v4 §B.3 recovery, but the dead-letter log will show a gap). Any audit trail entries in .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json also become stale artifacts referencing a reverted feature.
findings.remediation: (a) Add TickOutcome::DriftExcluded { excluded_accounts: Vec<(AccountId, DriftReport)>, eligible_count: usize } so the failure mode is observable. (b) Add a minimum_eligible_accounts: usize field to SupervisorConfig (default 1); if eligible_count < minimum_eligible_accounts after drift exclusion, emit a supervisor_drift_blackhole_total metric and return TickOutcome::DriftExcluded rather than silently passing an empty slice to RoutePolicy. (c) Add acceptance row C.32: if all accounts drift and VerifyMode::FailOnDrift, tick_once returns DriftExcluded (not Err(NoEligibleAccount)), and supervisor_drift_blackhole_total increments.

findings.title: AccountSnapshotProvider empty-Vec is semantically ambiguous post-v5; no observable exclusion signal
findings.evidence: v5 §B.4 extends AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() semantics without changing the trait signature: 'The trait signature fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<ProviderAccount> is unchanged.' Pre-v5, an empty Vec means no accounts are registered. Post-v5, an empty Vec can also mean 'all accounts drift-excluded.' Code that was written against the v4 contract (empty Vec = no accounts) silently gets the new semantics. If v5 is reverted, the old provider re-appears, which re-hides any drift that was being filtered — accounts that drifted during v5's deployment window are now silently eligible again without reconciliation.
artifact_refs: v5-§B.4: 'trait signature unchanged' + exclusion-on-drift semantic extension
v4-§B.4 step 2: 'let accounts = self.accounts.snapshot()' — no empty-Vec guard downstream
v5-§B.5: settings-drift-report.json written to .omc/state/ — runtime artifact, not committed
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: Reverting v5 means drift exclusion stops. Accounts that the renderer had identified as drifted are now silently eligible for routing again (their dotfiles may still have the bad/renderer-written settings). The .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json artifact remains but is no longer updated, creating a stale audit artifact.
findings.remediation: Add an optional companion method to AccountSnapshotProvider (default impl returns None) — fn last_exclusion_reasons(&self) -> Option<Vec<(AccountId, DriftReport)>>. SupervisorApp::tick_once calls this after snapshot() and emits supervisor_account_drift_excluded{account_id} gauge. This keeps observability without changing the trait contract and survives rollback gracefully (old impls return None, metric disappears cleanly).

findings.title: v4 crate additions + Cedar + registry/accounts/ + templates/ are fully reversible — not rollback concerns
findings.evidence: v4 §B.1: 4 new crates (supervisor-kernel, supervisor-app, jsonl-supervisor-adapter, supervisor-conformance). v5 §B.1: 2 new crates (settings-template-kernel, settings-template-adapter-fs). All are additive-only. Branch Y (v4 §A.1 principle 4): zero net-new external deps verified against Cargo.toml:481-492. v4 §B.2.6: lean-a10 declaration count = 0 new public APIs on existing kernels. docs/policies/foundry-supervisor.cedar (v4 §B.10): new file, rollback = delete. registry/accounts/ (v4 §B.10 patch #7): new directory, rollback = rm -rf. templates/foundry-supervisor/ (v5 §B.8): new directory, rollback = rm -rf. Phase M02-P06 carved (v4 §B.9): metadata only, does not block existing phase completion. SettingsTemplate.version u32 (v5 §B.2.1): applies only to new template files that do not yet exist on disk pre-merge.
artifact_refs: v4-§B.2.6: 'Lean-a10 declaration count: 0 new public APIs on existing kernels'
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: Nothing in existing code. Removal of 6 crates from Cargo.toml::members + deletion of their directories is the complete rollback. No downstream crate imports these new crates (they are leaves in the dependency graph as of v4+v5 scope). Cedar policy deletion removes supervisor-scoped rules; the umbrella autonomy-ceiling.cedar seed (3 lines, v4 §B.0) is untouched.
findings.remediation: No action required. Confirm v4 acceptance row C.15 (lean-a10 public-API snapshot byte-identical) is enforced in CI to catch any accidental existing-kernel surface mutation during execution.

rollback_playbook_gaps.gap: No documented 'undo-render' procedure for dotfile mutations (F10-02)

rollback_playbook_gaps.gap: No TickOutcome::DriftExcluded to distinguish drift-blackhole from no-accounts (F10-03)

forward_only_steps.rationale: Version field applies only to new template files in templates/foundry-supervisor/ which do not yet exist. No existing artifact tracks a previous version. A template version bump before any account is onboarded causes no forward-only lock. Becomes a concern after first production account is onboarded — document this boundary in the ADR.

InboxStore is a new trait in the new supervisor-kernel crate. No existing crate implements it. Adding dead_letter() is not a breaking change to any existing code. Rollback of supervisor-kernel removes the trait entirely.
